clue.text: Frank Yerby requires us to say something at once

definitions.meaning: a novel by the American writer Frank Yerby carries this title
an instruction to talk immediately, as at the 'or forever hold your peace' moment of a wedding

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the title of a Yerby novel; the other is an imperative urging immediate speech.

clue.text: Peak achievement of Scott

parts.note: reads as Scott's finest work, but points to the Walter Scott novel whose full title ends 'of the Peak'

explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott wrote a novel set in the Derbyshire Peak District whose hero gives it this name.

clue.text: "Steel-true and blade-straight,/ The great —— — / Made my mate." (Stevenson)

parts.words: "Steel-true and blade-straight,/ The great —— — / Made my mate." (Stevenson)
parts.note: a gap-fill from Robert Louis Stevenson's poem 'My Wife', where the missing word is a craftsman, here God as maker

explanation.surface: A line of Stevenson's love poem praising his wife as made by a master craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled maker or craftsman, Stevenson's image of the Creator fashioning his wife.

clue.text: Train traveller who obtained some help from Bradshaw

definitions.text: Train traveller who obtained some help from Bradshaw

parts.words: Train traveller who obtained some help from Bradshaw
parts.note: Bradshaw suggests the old railway timetable, but is the narrator William Bradshaw of Isherwood's novel about a man who changes trains

explanation.surface: A rail passenger consults the Victorian railway timetable for guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: Bradshaw was the famous British railway guide; in Isherwood's 'Mr Norris Changes Trains' the narrator Bradshaw helps the title character.
explanation.definitionFit: Isherwood's title character changes trains and is befriended and aided by the narrator Bradshaw.

clue.text: A good, fitting row upset amusing play (7, 3, )

explanation.surface: A suitable quarrel overturned makes for an entertaining piece of theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' tells you to rearrange the letters of A GOOD FITTING ROW.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett's tragicomedy is a stage play full of absurd humour.

clue.text: Where lads in their hundreds came in for the fair

definitions.text: Where lads in their hundreds came in for the fair

parts.words: Where lads in their hundreds came in for the fair
parts.note: echoes A. E. Housman's line 'The lads in their hundreds to — come in for the fair' from A Shropshire Lad

explanation.surface: Crowds of young men flock to a country fair.
explanation.walkthrough: The town is a market town in Shropshire, England, celebrated in Housman's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Housman's poem names this Shropshire market town as the destination of the fair-going lads.

clue.text: Lampedusa subject I found in fellow countryman poet

explanation.surface: An Italian novelist's theme is discovered in a poet from his own country.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Leopardi was an Italian poet, so a compatriot of the Sicilian Lampedusa.

clue.text: Pikes surrounding engineers in primitive Roman tribe

indicators.note: surrounding means the pike word goes round the engineers

parts.note: luce is an old word for the pike fish, plural luces
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: Spear-carriers encircle military engineers among an ancient people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pikes' suggests weapons, but it is the fish, luce.
explanation.definitionFit: This was one of the three original tribes into which early Rome's citizens were divided.

clue.text: Borrow book about reportedly unmanageable cetaceans (4, )

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: unmanageable means wild, and cetaceans are whales

explanation.surface: Borrow a book about uncontrollable whales, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borrow' looks like a verb but is George Borrow, the Victorian travel writer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Borrow's 1862 travel book recounts his walking tour through that country.

clue.text: Archetype selected from balaclava, tarboosh, fez etc

indicators.note: selected from means a run of letters is picked out of the headgear names

explanation.surface: A model chosen from a list of hats.
explanation.definitionFit: An embodiment or perfect example of a type.

clue.text: "They drink like Nectar, the — Encomiums that are made them."(Richard Burton)

parts.words: "They drink like Nectar, the — Encomiums that are made them."(Richard Burton)
parts.note: a gap-fill from Robert Burton's Anatomy of Melancholy, the missing adjective meaning mocking or not sincerely meant

explanation.surface: A quotation about people swallowing flattering praise as though it were nectar.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic form of a word meaning sardonic, saying one thing to mean its opposite.

clue.text: Anonymous manuscripts reaching a wide audience

definitions.text: Anonymous manuscripts reaching a wide audience

parts.words: Anonymous manuscripts reaching a wide audience
parts.note: sounds like unattributed handwritten works widely read, but means scrawled writing on public walls

explanation.surface: Unsigned writings that find a large readership.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsigned writing scrawled on walls is seen by every passer-by.

clue.text: Warden perhaps, or The Prince .

indicators.note: perhaps suggests an alternative version of the word warden, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Is it Trollope's The Warden, or Machiavelli's The Prince?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange the letters of WARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince of the British royal family, the Duke of York, bears this name.

clue.text: She went underground, received oracular instructions and was presented to royalty ()

definitions.text: She went underground, received oracular instructions and was presented to royalty

parts.words: She went underground, received oracular instructions and was presented to royalty
parts.note: describes Carroll's heroine: down the rabbit-hole, told 'Drink me' and 'Eat me', and brought before the Queen of Hearts

explanation.surface: A woman descends into the underworld, consults an oracle and meets a monarch, like a classical heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's girl falls down a rabbit-hole, obeys labels on bottles and cakes, and meets the King and Queen.

clue.text: Time and time again he wrote bedroom farce (joking apart)

definitions.text: Time and time again he wrote bedroom farce (joking apart)

parts.words: Time and time again he wrote bedroom farce (joking apart)
parts.note: reads as a writer forever producing farce, but strings together three play titles: Time and Time Again, Bedroom Farce, Joking Apart

explanation.surface: Seriously, this writer churned out bedroom farces over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Ayckbourn, the English dramatist, wrote all three plays named in the clue.

clue.text: Ancestral Christmas tree (a present from Norway)

definitions.text: Ancestral Christmas tree (a present from Norway)

parts.words: Ancestral Christmas tree (a present from Norway)
parts.note: plays on Norway's gift of a Christmas tree to London each year, pointing to the world tree of Norse mythology

explanation.surface: Norway sends Britain its annual Christmas tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Norway gives London's Trafalgar Square a Christmas tree every year; the answer is the giant ash of Norse myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The immense ash binding the worlds in Norse mythology, an ancient sacred tree from Scandinavian lore.

clue.text: Relative times, we hear, for J. C. Harris character (4, )

indicators.note: we hear means the next word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: tempi, plural of tempo, are musical times

explanation.surface: A relative's timings, apparently, for a figure in Joel Chandler Harris's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A character in Harris's Uncle Remus tales.

clue.text: Printer's assistant, possibly? at scene of Allied victory

definitions.meaning: a man who inks the type for a printer
the 1854 Crimean War battle won by British and French forces over the Russians

explanation.surface: A print-shop helper turns up at a famous battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, it describes an inking man; whole, it is the Crimean battle site.

clue.text: Name of historian enshrined in code

definitions.text: Name of historian enshrined in code

parts.words: Name of historian enshrined in code
parts.note: the Earl who wrote History of the Rebellion also gave his title to a set of 1660s laws against Nonconformists

explanation.surface: A historian's name is written into a legal code.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Hyde, Earl of Clarendon, historian of the Civil War, lends his title to the Clarendon Code of statutes.

clue.text: "I'd learned to drive in the RAF. I'd shared an Austin Chummy with three of the " (John Braine)

parts.note: a gap-fill from John Braine's Room at the Top; the missing word is the flying crew members of an RAF bomber

clue.text: Disadvantages of horse in ship ()

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: The drawbacks of keeping a horse aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitches or drawbacks, the unforeseen problems in a plan.

clue.text: Go zonal, perhaps, to find Neapolitan councillor

indicators.note: perhaps hints that go zonal is one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Dividing into zones to locate a Naples official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange the letters of GO ZONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The honest old counsellor of Naples in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: His candidate was from north-eastern China

definitions.text: His candidate was from north-eastern China

parts.words: His candidate was from north-eastern China
parts.note: north-eastern China is Manchuria, pointing to the novel The Manchurian Candidate

explanation.surface: A politician fielded a nominee from north-east China.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Condon wrote the 1959 thriller The Manchurian Candidate.

clue.text: Playwright suggests prohibition to opening of Rievaulx Abbey

parts.note: a bar is a ban or prohibition

indicators.note: opening of means the first letters of the abbey's name are used

clue.text: Haunting hackwork

an is the indefinite article

clue.text: Woman novelist might be seen as novel chap
